title: Monthly booking demand
interpretation: Demand per run ranges from 186 (2024-09) to 359 (2026-05). Compare months on the top panel: the raw totals below mostly reflect which 32 runs were sampled.

title: Passenger volume per simulated run, by final status
interpretation: Passengers per run peak at 719 in 2026-05. Confirmed passengers are the largest block every month; Cancelled and Waitlisted passengers hold no seat at departure.

title: Cancellation rate by journey month
interpretation: Both rates move together around 13.8% (passenger-based, range 12.4% to 15.1%). The booking-based rate is lower because partially cancelled bookings are not counted as cancelled.

title: Waitlist demand, clearance and uncleared waitlist
y_axis: Share of passengers / of waitlist demand
interpretation: About 9.1% of passengers start waitlisted; only 19.2% clear to a seat, and 65.6% are still waitlisted at chart preparation and refunded.

title: Seat occupancy and waitlist pressure by journey month
interpretation: Occupancy averages 73.5% and ranges 58.4% to 92.0%; it never exceeds 100% because waitlisted passengers are excluded and shown separately as pressure.

title: Gross, refund and net booking value (INR)
interpretation: Refunds are 17.5% of gross booking value overall, so net is 82.5% of gross. Month-to-month swings in totals follow demand per run and the mix of sampled trains.

title: Train performance: the 8 lowest and 8 highest seat occupancy
interpretation: Occupancy ranges from 35.6% to 97.6% across 52 trains. Intervals of neighbouring trains overlap, so the exact ranking is indicative only; the gap between the two ends is large.

title: Route performance: the 15 routes with the most passengers per simulated run
interpretation: Busiest routes carry 897 passengers per run, versus 478 for the median route. High demand per run does not always mean high occupancy: routes also differ in seats per run.

title: Class performance: occupancy, waitlist pressure and cancellation by travel class
interpretation: Occupancy is highest in 3A (76.8%) and lowest in CC (52.5%); cancellation is lowest in 1A (8.1%). Classes differ in the number of simulated class-runs (labels).

title: Status distribution: passengers by class and bookings overall
interpretation: 72.6% of bookings end fully Confirmed and 2.3% Mixed. Share of passengers who end Confirmed varies by class from 71% to 88%.

title: Fare per passenger: distribution overall and by class
interpretation: The distribution is right-skewed: mean INR 1,513 sits above the median INR 1,053, because premium classes and long routes pull the tail. Class explains much of the spread.

title: Weekday and weekend comparison
interpretation: Weekend-day runs average 500 passengers vs 536 on weekdays, but intervals overlap widely: the gap is not statistically distinguishable from zero (test S-01, Welch p = 0.054; Mann-Whitney p is larger).

title: Cancellation rate by booking lead time
interpretation: Cancellation rises with lead time: booking-based 9.3% (0-3 days) to 21.4% (61-120 days); chi-square test p < 0.001, Cramer's V = 0.11 (small-to-moderate). This is an association in synthetic data built with such a pattern, not evidence that early booking causes cancellation.

title: Distribution of seat occupancy across simulated train-class runs
interpretation: 31.2% of class-runs are at or above 95% occupancy while 20.0% are below 50%: the average (73.6%) hides a wide spread between full and under-used runs.

title: Correlation between run-level measures (Spearman)
interpretation: The strongest pair is occupancy / initial waitlist passengers (rho = 0.79); several links are mechanical (occupancy is built from passengers and seats). Arrival delay is essentially uncorrelated with demand (|rho| <= 0.05). Correlation is not causation.

title: Punctuality by season
interpretation: Overall on-time performance is 74.8%. Seasonal differences are small: delay p = 0.08 (Kruskal-Wallis), on-time share p = 0.21 (chi-square), neither significant; with 124 to 249 runs per season, only large differences would be detectable.
